name: Jian
dietDetails: Carnivorous predator with ziphodont dentition adapted for shearing flesh.
discoveryHistory:
• The jian (simplified Chinese: 剑; traditional Chinese: 劍, Mandarin Chinese: [tɕjɛ̂n], Cantonese: [kim˧], English approximation:  jyehn) is a Chinese term referring to all double-edged straight sword.
• Holotype excavated from the Fossil-bearing formation (China).
• Cataloged and classified within Theropoda based on peer-reviewed diagnostic features.
interestingFacts: ["The jian (simplified Chinese: 剑; traditional Chinese: 劍, Mandarin Chinese: [tɕjɛ̂n], Cantonese: [kim˧], English approximation:  jyehn) is a Chinese term referring to all double-edged straight sword.","Professional jian practitioners, who were often romanticized in historical records, folklores and wuxia literature, are referred to as jianshi (Chinese: 劍士; pinyin: jiànshì; lit. 'swordsman') or jianke (Chinese: 劍客; pinyin: jiànkè; lit. 'sword guests', a term dating from the Han dynasty referring to retainers or warriors errant skilled in swordfighting).","The first Chinese recorded sources that mention the jian date to the 7th century BCE during the Spring and Autumn period, with one of the earliest archaeological specimens being the famed Sword of Goujian.","Early jian were made of bronze, which remained prevalent to as late as the Qin dynasty, but by the early Western Han dynasty bronze jian were largely supplanted by later ones made of carbon steel due to advancements in ironworking."]

name: Anzu
dietDetails: Carnivorous predator with ziphodont dentition adapted for shearing flesh.
discoveryHistory:
• Discovered in the Hell Creek Formation across North and South Dakota, United States.
• Based on three partial skeletons preserving skull material, cervical vertebrae, and limb bones.
• Formally described in 2014 by Emma Schachner, Matthew Lamanna, and colleagues.
interestingFacts: ["Anzu is an extinct genus of large caenagnathid oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation of North and South Dakota, United States.","Colloquially nicknamed the \"chicken from hell\", Anzu reached an estimated length of 3 to 3.5 meters and weighed around 200 to 300 kilograms.","Possessed a tall, paper-thin skull crest, a toothless keratinous beak, and long arms ending in slender curved talons adapted for omnivorous feeding.","Coexisted in the floodplains of Laramidia alongside famous contemporaries including Tyrannosaurus rex, Triceratops, and Edmontosaurus."]

name: Tiamat
dietDetails: Herbivorous high-browsing sauropod equipped with peg-like teeth for stripping foliage.
discoveryHistory:
• In ancient Mesopotamian religion, Tiamat is the cosmic ocean that mates with Abzû, the groundwater, to produce the Babylonian pantheon in the creation myth recorded in the Enūma Eliš ("When on High").
• Holotype excavated from the Fossil-bearing formation (United States).
• Cataloged and classified within Theropoda based on peer-reviewed diagnostic features.
interestingFacts: ["In ancient Mesopotamian religion, Tiamat is the cosmic ocean that mates with Abzû, the groundwater, to produce the Babylonian pantheon in the creation myth recorded in the Enūma Eliš (\"When on High\").","Tiamat is referred to as a woman, and has – at various points in the epic – a number of anthropomorphic features such as breasts and theriomorphic features such as a tail.","In the Enūma Eliš, written in the 2nd millennium BCE in Lower Mesopotamia in the Babylonian variety of the Akkadian language, Tiamat gives birth to the first generation of deities after mingling her waters with those of Abzû.","The gods continue to reproduce, forming a new and noisy mass of divine children."]
sizeNotes: Medium-sized titanosaur estimated at 13.0–15.0 m in length and 8,000–10,000 kg mass.

interestingFacts: ["A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented at the beginning of the 20th century originally to explain malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes and their operators.","Depictions of these creatures vary widely.","Stories about them and references to them as the causes of especially inexplicable technical and mental problems of pilots were especially popular during and after World War II.","Use of the term in the sense of a mischievous creature that sabotages aircraft first arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots stationed in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s, with the earliest printed record in a poem published in the journal Aeroplane in Malta on 10 April 1929."]
sizeNotes: Small hornless ceratopsian measuring approximately 1.5–1.8 m in length and 30–45 kg mass.

interestingFacts: ["Zuul is an extinct genus of herbivorous ankylosaurine dinosaur from the Campanian Judith River Formation of Montana.","The type species is Zuul crurivastator.","It is known from a complete skull and tail, which represents the first ankylosaurin known from a complete skull and tail club, as well as the most complete ankylosaurid specimen thus far recovered from North America.","The specimen also preserved in situ osteoderms, keratin, and skin remains."]
